title: One Seamless Workflow With Clo-Set: Render, Mix&Match
description:
CLO-SET is a cloud-based platform that enables users to collaborate easily with the entire clothing-making process through 3D file management, sharing, and real-time communication.

Render realistic visuals and mix-and-match styling options before anything goes into production.

- Visit CLO-SET https://style.clo-set.com/aboutus
- Join Discord: https://discord.com/invite/G2eaK3PDSu
- For any questions, visit https://clo-set-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us
transcript: In this lesson, we will learn how to visualize designs through rendering and explore styling options using Mix and Match. First, click the Render button on the left side of the viewer in the Content page. In the Render settings, you can configure options such as colorway, image format, size, background, and quality. You can also save your settings as a preset to maintain consistency across renders. Once you've finished the render settings, click the Render button to start rendering. On the left side of the viewer, you can check the rendering status. Once it's complete, you can start rendering. Click the rendered image to view the results, and you can also download it for further review. Next, let's organize the styles for review using Assortment and try Mix and Match. First, create an assortment from the top left of your brand workspace. Then, select styles based on their workflow status and organize them into the assortment. Once you've added all the content for review, go to the assortment. Within the assortment, you can view only the selected content. You can also switch between 2D view, 3D view, and render view, depending on your needs. Now, click the Mix and Match button at the top right to start reviewing different combinations. Select multiple items and drag and drop them into the viewer. Use the Gizmo tool to adjust and position the garments. Once your layout is ready, use the Save Scene feature to export it as an image. Review different combinations by mixing and matching multiple items. After the review, pin the adopted colorway and leave comments to share feedback.
markdown_content: ## Render a Design: Configure Render Settings and Generate Images This section covers using the **Render** workflow in the Content page, configuring render parameters (e.g., colorway, format, size, background, quality), and saving/downloading the rendered output. 1. Open the **Content** page. 2. Click the **Render** button on the **left side** of the viewer. 3. In **Render settings**, configure: - **Colorway** - **Image format** - **Size** - **Background** - **Quality** 4. (Optional) Save your configuration as a **preset** to keep render settings consistent across multiple renders. 5. Click **Render** to start rendering. 6. Monitor **rendering status** on the **left side** of the viewer. 7. When rendering completes: - Click the **rendered image** to view results. - **Download** the image for further review. ## Organize Styles for Review with Assortment (2D/3D/Render Views) This section explains how to create and manage an **Assortment** so you can review selected styles, and how to switch between **2D**, **3D**, and **render view**. 1. Create an assortment from the **top left** of your brand workspace. 2. Select styles based on their **workflow status**. 3. Add the selected styles/content into the assortment for review. 4. Open the **assortment** to view only the selected content. 5. Switch views as needed: - **2D view** - **3D view** - **Render view** ## Review Combinations with Mix and Match (Gizmo, Save Scene, Pin & Comments) This section covers using **Mix and Match** to test different item combinations, arranging garments with the **Gizmo** tool, exporting layouts via **Save Scene**, and capturing feedback by pinning and commenting. 1. Click the **Mix and Match** button at the **top right** to begin reviewing combinations. 2. Select **multiple items**. 3. **Drag and drop** the selected items into the viewer. 4. Use the **Gizmo** tool to **adjust and position** the garments. 5. When the layout is ready, use **Save Scene** to export it as an **image**. 6. Review different combinations by repeatedly mixing and matching multiple items. 7. After review: - **Pin** the adopted **colorway**. - Leave **comments** to share feedback.
